# Weekly tax table
## On this page
- [Working out the withholding amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-table-weekly#ato-Workingoutthewithholdingamount)
- [Leave payments and termination payments made to employees](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-table-weekly#ato-Leavepaymentsandterminationpaymentsmadetoemployees)
- [Leave loading](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-table-weekly#ato-Leaveloading)
- [PAYG withholding publications](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-table-weekly#ato-PAYGwithholdingpublications)

## Using this tax table
- use the [Withholding lookup tool (XLSX, 26KB)This link will download a file](https://www.ato.gov.au/api/public/content/9f1eef6f5ed8415e8e9da14004e094a2?v=5526fbcd) This link will download a file to quickly work out the amount to withhold

## Working out the withholding amount
2. Input the amount from step 1 into the [Withholding lookup tool (XLSX, 26KB)This link will download a file](https://www.ato.gov.au/api/public/content/9f1eef6f5ed8415e8e9da14004e094a2?v=5526fbcd), as per instructions in the tool.
3. Use the appropriate column to find the correct amount to withhold. If your payee is
   - claiming the tax-free threshold, use column 2
   - not claiming the tax-free threshold, use column 3.
4. If your payee has an entitlement to a tax offset, use the [Ready reckoner for tax offsets](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-table-weekly#readyreckoner) to convert the payee's estimate of their full-year entitlement into a weekly offset value. Then subtract this value from the withholding amount found in step 3.
5. If your payee is entitled to make an adjustment for the Medicare levy, subtract the value of the adjustment, determined from the [Medicare levy adjustment weekly tax table](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/medicare-levy-adjustment-weekly-tax-table) from the amount found in step 4.

## Leave payments and termination payments made to employees
### Employees who continue working for you
You must include holiday pay (including any leave loading) and long service leave payments as part of normal earnings, except when they are paid on termination of employment.

For more information, refer to [Withholding from leave payments for continuing employees](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding/payments-you-need-to-withhold-from/payments-to-employees/withholding-from-leave-payments-for-continuing-employees).

## Leave loading
If you pay leave loading as a lump sum, use [Schedule 5 – Tax table for back payments, commissions, bonuses and similar payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/schedule-5-tax-table-for-back-payments-commissions-bonuses-and-similar-payments) to calculate withholding.

If you pay leave loading on a pro-rata basis, add the leave loading payment to earnings for that period to calculate withholding.

## PAYG withholding publications
- [PAYG withholding](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding)

# Tax tables
Use these quick links to find the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding tax tables.

## About tax tables
We produce a range of tax tables to help you work out how much to withhold from payments you make to your employees or other payees. A [tax withheld calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/tax-withheld-calculator) that calculates the correct amount of tax to withhold is available.

## Tax tables that were updated and apply from 1 July 2026

web.description:
# Tax withheld calculator
## Go to the calculator
### Tax withheld for individuals calculator
This calculator works out the amount of tax to withhold from payments made to employees (payees) and other workers, including working holiday makers.

## Tax withheld for individuals calculator instructions
### Payments
Other [tax tables](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-tables-overview) apply for these workers.

### Leave loading
If you pay leave loading as a lump sum, you need to use [Tax table for back payments, commissions, bonuses and similar payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/schedule-5-tax-table-01-july-2025-to-30-june-2026) to calculate withholding.

If you pay leave loading on a pro rata basis, then add the leave loading payment to earnings for the period to calculate withholding.

### Terms we use
#### Tax file number not provided
- the whole amount of all leave loading payments
- payments on termination of employment – that is, holiday pay, unused annual leave and long service leave

web.title: Tax table for unused leave payments on termination of employment
web.description:
# Schedule 7 – Tax table for unused leave payments on termination of employment
## On this page
- [Working out the withholding amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-7-tax-table-for-unused-leave-payments-on-termination-of-employment#ato-Workingoutthewithholdingamount)
- [PAYG withholding publications](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-7-tax-table-for-unused-leave-payments-on-termination-of-employment#ato-PAYGwithholdingpublications)

## Using this schedule
Before calculating the amount to be withheld, you must work out if the payments are being made as a result of a genuine redundancy, invalidity or an early retirement scheme.

For more information, refer to [Withholding from unused leave payments on termination of employment](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/employment-termination-payments-withholding-from-unused-leave-payments).

## Working out the withholding amount
### When a tax file number (TFN) is provided
| Payment type | Reason | Accrual dates | Withholding rates | Payment summary label or equivalent in STP |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Long service leave | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Pre-16 August 1978 | 5% of total at marginal rates | B |
| Long service leave | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | 16 August 1978 to 17 August 1993 | 32% | A |
| Long service leave | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Post-17 August 1993 | Marginal rates | Include in salary/wages |
| Long service leave | Termination because of genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme | Pre-16 August 1978 | 5% of total at marginal rates | B |
| Long service leave | Termination because of genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme | 16 August 1978 to 17 August 1993 | 32% | A |
| Long service leave | Termination because of genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme | Post-17 August 1993 | 32% | A |
| Annual leave | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Pre-18 August 1993 | 32% | A |
| Annual leave | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Post-17 August 1993 | Marginal rates | Include in salary/wages |
| Annual leave | Termination because of genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme | Any date | 32% | A |
| Annual leave loading | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Pre-18 August 1993 | 32% | A |
| Annual leave loading | Normal termination (e.g. voluntary resignation, employment terminated due to inefficiency, retirement) | Post-17 August 1993 | Marginal rates | Include in salary/wages |
| Annual leave loading | Termination because of genuine redundancy, invalidity or early retirement scheme | Any date | 32% | A |

Withholding amounts for long service leave, annual leave and annual leave loading

### When a TFN has not been provided
If your employee who is receiving the unused leave payments has not provided you with their TFN before the payment is made, you must withhold 47% from the payment.

If your employee is a foreign resident who has not provided you with their TFN, you must withhold 45% from the payment.

If your employee believes that for their circumstances the amount you withhold will be too much, they may apply for a variation to reduce the amount of withholding.

Your employee can refer to [Varying your PAYG withholding](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/jobs-and-employment-types/varying-your-payg-withholding) for more information.

## PAYG withholding publications
You can access all PAYG withholding tax tables and other PAYG withholding publications at:

- [Tax tables](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-tables-overview)
- [PAYG withholding](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding)

web.description:
# Allowances, leave and other payments
Withholding for allowances, leave and other payments.

## On this page
- [Leave loading](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-1-statement-of-formulas-for-calculating-amounts-to-be-withheld/allowances-leave-and-other-payments#ato-Leaveloading)
- [Leave payments and termination payments made to employees](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-1-statement-of-formulas-for-calculating-amounts-to-be-withheld/allowances-leave-and-other-payments#ato-Leavepaymentsandterminationpaymentsmadetoemployees)

## Leave loading
If you pay leave loading to an employee as a lump sum, use [Schedule 5 – Tax table for back payments, commissions, bonuses and similar payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/schedule-5-tax-table-for-back-payments-commissions-bonuses-and-similar-payments) to calculate withholding.

If you pay leave loading on a pro-rata basis, add the leave loading payment to earnings for that period to calculate withholding.

## Leave payments and termination payments made to employees
### Employees who continue working for you
For more information, see [Withholding from leave payments for continuing employees](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding/payments-you-need-to-withhold-from/payments-to-employees/withholding-from-leave-payments-for-continuing-employees).

### Employees who stop working for you
If an employee has unused annual leave, leave loading or long service leave, refer to [Schedule 7 – Tax table for unused leave payments on termination of employment](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-7-tax-table-for-unused-leave-payments-on-termination-of-employment).

Any other lump sum payments may be employment termination payments, refer to [Schedule 11 – Tax table for employment termination payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/payg-withholding-schedule-11-tax-table-for-employment-termination-payments).

Don't withhold any amount for study and training support loans debt from lump sum termination payments.
